10157105:
Ardagh

Ardagh is the northernmost settlement of the Ustalavic county of Odranto, located on the Moutray River, hard against the unforgiving lands of the Worldwound.⁠⁠
20984175:
Hemachandra

The Hemachandra, also known as the "Seat of the Golden Moon", is a legendary adventuring site in the eastern Divine Garden region of Vudra.⁠⁠ The terraced tower contains a shrine to each of the thousands of deities of the Vudran pantheon, from hundreds of minor gods on its lowest level to Irori alone on its highest level nearly a day's climb upward. Acolytes and priests live in some of the tower's middle levels.⁠
34724775:
Ice Spire

Ice Spire is a vast dungeon located in the northern plains of the Thanelands in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠⁠⁠⁠
44945045:
Storval Stairs

Built thousands of years ago by the enslaved giants of the Thassilonian empire,⁠ the Storval Stairs are a set of stair-like tiers carved into the side of the western Storval Rise, then part of Shalast.⁠ Although sized for a gigantic creature, they are by far the easiest way to cross the Rise west of the Iron Peaks. It is not uncommon for the Storval Rise to reach heights of over 1,000 feet in many places, sharply delineating the fertile lowlands from the barren scrub land of the Storval Plateau. At the Storval Stairs, however, the Rise is only 400 feet in height with human-sized steps and ramps cut into the gargantuan ones, making the passage even easier.⁠ Immense statues of the runelord Karzoug flank the Stairs, although the southern-most one is beginning to finally crumble due to erosion.⁠⁠
64341535:
City of Bone and Juniper

The City of Bone and Juniper is a taiga giant settlement in the mountains of Zi Ha in Tian Xia.⁠

The giants believe they are descendants of an underworld dragon and an ancient samsaran noble who sought to escape the cycle of rebirth to remain with her beloved.⁠ They keep the remains of their samsaran progenitor in a golden mausoleum on a hidden plateau marked by three towers made of wood and bone high in the mountains that happens to be located at the intersection of two ley lines, which provide the plateau special magical properties.⁠ Anyone who dares approach the mausoleum will be slain.⁠

The taiga giants spend most of the time dressed in red and black, but occasionally honor the samsaran noble by dressing in mottled blue and white. During the latter times they travel peacefully to the lowlands to trade with the human and samsaran villagers, all the while maintaining a strict code of silence.⁠

Adamas,⁠ also known as The Gleaming Tower, is a white marble tower a few miles from Olfden that rises out of the ground at the base of the Elberwick Rise.⁠

House Beumhal

House Beumhal is located in south-western Odranto, one of the counties of Ustalav.⁠⁠⁠
81242965:
Gao Bie

Gao Bie (pronounced gau-bier),⁠ also spelled Gau Bie, is a large town in the Sun Shogunate of Songbai⁠⁠ that serves as a waystation for land and river trade routes. Its name is derived from the Tien phrase for "goodbye".⁠

During peacetime Gao Bie hosts traders and furloughed soldiers, and the town's lack of security despite its strategic location also draws criminals and adventurers.⁠

Monolith Glacier

The Monolith Glacier is located near the north-westernmost corner of the Thanelands in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings; it is formed in the western reaches of the high Stormspear Mountains range and is slowly moving southwards. The Monolith Glacier has a distinct, very symmetrical oblong shape and those few brave explorers who have ventured up onto the glacier report seeing a large fortress entombed within the very heart of the glacier. Monolith Glacier is a very dangerous place to explore: blizzards often engulf it; its surface is riddled with crevasses and ice tunnels created by the numerous deadly remorhazes that live in the glacier's depths. Unbeknownst to everyone, the glacier is a sentient elemental that speaks with a voice of grinding ice and might be willing to allow access to the strange structure at its heart to anyone who can rid it of the pesky remorhazes infesting it.⁠⁠
92356265:
Staviancara

Staviancara is the oldest inhabited building in Westcrown, having been built by Taldan slaves, which gives it a military architecture with secret tunnels beneath. It is located in Rego Laina and now serves as the residence of the regidottari commander of the city.⁠

Ishad

Ishad is one of the numerous large, prosperous cities that dot the fertile Qadiran region of Pashman. It is located on the banks of the Pashman River along Pashman's south-western border with the neighbouring region of Tapur.⁠⁠
117978505:
Castle Firrine

Castle Firrine is an abandoned castle located just south of Ghostlight Marsh, at the edge of the Gravelands in what was once the nation of Lastwall.⁠⁠
119784365:
Fort Ramgate

Fort Ramgate is a frontier town of the nation of Molthune, in the Marideth River valley.⁠ It has impressive fortifications, which are tested on an almost daily basis by the forces of neighboring Nirmathas. In fact, the town takes its name from the repeated attempts to destroy its gates. Despite this, the town's population continues to grow, as Molthune's Imperial Army concentrates its forces here in preparation for the almost inevitable invasion of Nirmathas. Indeed, most of the few elite troops of the Imperial Army are currently stationed in Fort Ramgate.⁠

The town is commanded by General Hakar.⁠ General Lord Resper Cyrno ostensibly rules the Border region of Molthune from Fort Ramgate as its territorial seat, but spends very little time there.⁠
132033335:
Kintargo Keep

Kintargo Keep is a part of the larger Castle Kintargo that dominates the Castle District of the city of Kintargo. The keep's five-storey spire juts from the north-western corner of the castle, and under the rule of Cheliax it served as Kintargo's most notorious prison.⁠⁠ As of 4724 AR under independent Ravounel, it had been sealed since the Ruby Massacre in 4716 AR.⁠
132333865:
Ul-Angorn

Ul-Angorn is a small town on the Crown of the World, lying on the shores of Saltsea Lake. It is the largest settlement of Erutaki humans in the Ruun Uvas basin. Ul-Angorn is a resting spot for caravans along the Path of Aganhei between the High Ice⁠ and Ovorikheer Pass.⁠

Ul-Angorn is prosperous for a town its size, and its inhabitants are inquisitive and garrulous.⁠
149459015:
Ipeq

Located along the banks of the Crook River, Ipeq (pronounced ahy-PECK)⁠ is the third-largest city in southern Osirion. According to legend, Ipeq was conjured into existence in a single day by Pharaoh An-Hepsu VII.⁠⁠⁠⁠ Ipeq stands on the southern bank of the river and completely blocks the Shallows of Ipeq, one of only three ways of crossing the Crook on foot.⁠⁠
150265905:
Chorak's Tomb

A small island in Lake Skotha on Varisia's Storval Plateau, Chorak's Tomb is sacred to the region's giants. Many believed that it was the last outpost of a once-great giant civilization dating back thousands of years. However, all trespassers are driven away by bombardments of boulders and rune-covered ballista bolts⁠⁠ fired by stone giant guardians of the site.⁠

The tomb is the resting place of Chorak, a gigas. In 4724 AR, the tomb was struck by a warshard that awakened Chorak and began disabling the tomb's wards, despite the efforts of its stone giant guardians.⁠
164404105:
Crevasse Fields

The Crevasse Fields are a glacial fissure in northern Irrisen, avoided by all travelers. It stretches 25 miles wide and 75 miles long, a expanse of pure ice and cliffs. No one would normally venture into the area, but powerful magic can be detected there, suggesting some kind of artifact is responsible for the region's instability and rumors abound that it was left by the gods, or perhaps by Baba Yaga, to plunge Irrisen into an eternal winter. Because of this, many adventurers have explored the region, and while some return with tales of treasure, none have come back with an answer to the mystery of the ice's power. To make matters worse, a traveler must also contend with the Crevasse Fields' inhabitants: will-o'-wisps, at least three linnorms, and a wendigo said to devour souls.⁠
175689395:
Humbright House

Humbright House was one of a number of smaller shrines to Aroden that once dotted Kintargo's Temple Hill district but has been abandoned since the god's death.⁠⁠
180248725:
Menhemes Manor

The Menhemes Manor stands against the wall facing Absalom in Westgate, the home of one of the city's oldest noble families. House Menhemes has constructed several black pyramids, a corridor lined with sphinx statues, and sand gardens that showcase their lineage to the nation of Osirion, but what is most striking is their extensive library containing archives thousands of years old, managed by the brilliant Scion Lord Rogren Sphairo.⁠
182554125:
Aaramor

The city-fortress of Aaramor is located on the southern banks of the West Sellen River in northwestern Numeria, near the edge of Sarkoris.⁠
187770705:
Godsmouth Cathedral


The Godsmouth Cathedral is the centre of worship of Pharasma in Kaer Maga, Varisia. It is located in the Bottoms district of the city just above the Godsmouth Ossuary. The cathedral is led by Delana Karaheis, High Priestess of Death, who is ably supported by the High Priestess of Birth, Maris Jelasco, and less ably supported by the High Priest of Fate, Mahajan Sandeep⁠

Other staff include Cryptsmistress Valanthe Nerissia.⁠

The Cathedral includes a chapel to Saint Illiska.⁠
189353315:
House of Sky

The House of Sky is an aerie high in the Five Kings Range that is the home of the giant owls of the Fierani Forest. These intelligent creatures have been allied with the elves of Kyonin for millennia, but are quite mistrustful of any other humanoid who makes the dangerous trek to their home. They hate Treerazer and his demonic minions, and can be summoned by the rulers of Kyonin in times of need via enchanted whistles. They are led by Winglord Kreiagh, who oversees a council of owls who frequently disagree with one another, but whose every word is taken to heart. Travel to the House of Sky is quite dangerous on foot, and is most easily accomplished by flight.⁠
190028505:
Raschka-Tor

Raschka-Tor is the lair of the most fearsome family of red dragons in the entire Hold of Belkzen. The family consists of four red dragons, two still only wyrmlings. They were one of the greatest threats to anyone traveling across northern Belkzen until the idea of leaving them tribute at Covenant Rock caught on. The dragons live in a mountainside cave known as Raschka-Tor which is orc for fire mountain. Rumour has it that their lair is in fact just the entrance to a vast city carved within the mountain itself. However, due to the dragons' dislike of nosy adventurers, no one has yet been able to verify these rumours.⁠
214114245:
Wizard's Grace

Wizard's Grace is an inn and tavern near Breachill Town Hall, in the south-east of the Isgeri town, making it a popular stop for both adventurers and locals. Its friendly atmosphere is largely due to the efforts of its innkeeper, Trinil Uskwold, the granddaughter of a local adventurer. Being so close to the town center, the clientele is generally well-mannered, and adventurers and council members often chat over meals. It is also a common rendezvous spot for those seeking employment through the council's monthly Call for Heroes, when Trinil serves her traditional boar-and-lentil stew.⁠

Our Lady of Blessed Waters

Our Lady of Blessed Waters is a monument rising out of the Seerspring Garden in Magnimar's Keystone district. Nobody knows who built this bronze statue of woman who many believe is a spirit living in the Seerspring. Religious scholars maintain they can concentrate better after spending time studying the statue.⁠
242458395:
Silent Partner

The Silent Partner is an unassuming shop in the Oriat district whose main business is lending money to those who don't meet the requirements of the Abadar church in the city. Its loans carry much higher interest rates than normal, and its main clients are adventurers whose treasure hunts are enough to repay their debts. Angston the Lender deal with those who fail to make their payments by sending a team of collectors that hunt them down and who will sell everything the clients own to settle the debt, including their lives.⁠
242528815:
Orlendas

Orlendas has been destroyed and rebuilt over a dozen times in its history. Plagues, fires, wars, and centaur hordes have all been the cause of Orlendas' fall at least once, but the town's importance to Orlov and Franax as a source of timber for their shipbuilding industries has kept settlers returning. The demand for lumber has waned over the years, but, along with small pelts, it still remains one of the town's primary imports.

The town's current komar, Galtan ranger Kasrel Unilich, has brought investment to the town, and Orlendas is now better defended and more prosperous than at any point in its history.⁠

Black Tarn

Black Tarn is an infamous mountain lake on the Ironbound Island of Dragon's Rib in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠

Ovorikheer Pass

Ovorikheer Pass is part of the Path of Aganhei as it descends from the high ice of the Crown of the World into the catchment basin of Ruun Uvas in Tian Xia.⁠⁠
284410295:
Breachill

Breachill is a small town in eastern Isger, in the foothills of the Five Kings Mountains.⁠⁠
287112605:
Castle Issono

Castle Issono is part of the eastern wall of the Chelaxian city of Corentyn. Most foot traffic comes through its gates, then passes through Easttown and the Noble Quarters, and accesses the harbor.⁠

The Castle Issono is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
292349615:
Blacknape Hideout

Blacknape Hideout is located on one of the islands in the Westchannel, where a gang of thugs, the Blacknapes, released from prison in 4710 AR by the Council of Thieves, gathered to wreak havoc. The group specialized in kidnapping children and the elderly, who were easy to hold prisoner and could demand ransoms for their safe return.⁠
295131875:
Lost Mine of Siwat

The Lost Mine of Siwat is a lost silver mine located in the Sahure Wastes of central Osirion. It was originally founded in 4349 AR, but mysteriously disappeared only a few years thereafter. Few people today even remember that the silver mine, and the small village of Siwat that grew up around it, ever existed.⁠⁠
295417145:
Glass Pyramids

The Glass Pyramids are a pair of transparent pyramids located in the Inner City district of Katapesh. The pyramids are made of transparent metal plates, a unique design created by Gezbria and Tralvar, the two dwarven wizards interred within who had arrived to Katapesh in 2219 AR.

Unknown to almost all, the two wizards discovered a confluence of magic ley lines beneath the Golden City and built two structures atop it, but too late realised that the magic was corrupt and uncontrollable. To stop this powerful magic being used for evil they built the Glass Pyramids on top of their previous structures, and after warding themselves with powerful magic they interred themselves alive within the pyramids. The magic of the corrupted ley lines soon overwhelmed them, transforming them into evil liches.

The site is regularly investigated by curious adventurers and scholars, but those smart enough to bypass the magic wards inevitably fall victim to the evil liches dwelling within.⁠ The Glassclaw tribe of kobolds consider it their sacred mission to ensure that no one ever breaks the Glass Pyramids, claiming to have guarded the structures for more than 100 generations, a longer span of time than the pyramids have existed.⁠
295974145:
Ayajinbo

Ayajinbo is capital of the elven nation of Jinin in Tian Xia, and stewards of the Silver Tree, the Darklands entrance that elves used in millennia past to reach the continent. It is renowned for its gardens, well-crafted stone buildings, and extensive dawnsilver trade.⁠
306073135:
Lost Mines

The Lost Mines once dug deep into the roots of the Mindspin Mountains on the western border of Nirmathas. They, and all their miners, suddenly disappeared in an unexplained occurrence.⁠
311145125:
Jacovo's Stables

Jacovo's Stables is a small ranch near town where good-quality horses are sold or loaned. Its owner, Jacovo, is an honest man with a good attitude who is helped in his business by his nephew, Gorvio.⁠⁠
315628005:
M'neri Valley Cattle Ranch

M'neri Valley Cattle Ranch began as a cattle ranch on the edge of the M'neri Plains in Sargava. It was established by Olgran Macini under the name Freehold as a holiday spot, but has since grown into the equivalent of a small town. Olgan always tried to be fair to the native Mwangi ranch hands, and since then they have been paid a fair wage and offered a share of the profits.⁠

It is currently run by Olgran's great-great-granddaughter Mindra Macini, although her cousin Salgarth is trying to gain control. He would like to run it as a "normal" Sargavan business, without any benefits for the Mwangi workers.⁠⁠⁠

In the aftermath of Sargava's fall and the establishment of Vidrian, Freehold was renamed to M'neri Cattle Ranch, while Mindra appointed two native siblings who work as a herder and breeder to handle daily operations.⁠ Some members of the Combined Mercantile Interests and Field Unions say Mindra should waive all of her claims if she believes the Mwangi to be her equals, while certain people who wish to bring back colonial rule seek to harshly punish Mindra and her ranch.⁠
315906655:
Korradath

The Korradath is the former royal castle and seat of Imperial Cheliax in the Rego Corna section of Westcrown. A massive fortified castle, it remains an impressive sight even though it has not seen any major upkeep since before the death of King Gaspodar in Neth of 4622 AR. It is still used by Wiscrani nobles for offices, temporary lodgings, or neutral meeting places for visitors to Westcrown that need to be impressed and protected from the rabble of the streets.⁠
322739005:
Occarin

Occarin is a village in the Carpenden Plains region of Andoran whose inhabitants are unknowingly and secretly almost all changeling children of three green hags.⁠
327787725:
Zar Kragnaral

Zar Kragnaral is located in the Stormspear Mountains in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. The legendary black basalt and blue ice fortress is ruled by the so-called Deathless Jarl.⁠⁠

Zar Kragnaral is an imposing structure nearly seven hundred feet in height. Its windows are made of hard ice and its towers are built of black rock. Delicate bridges of ice connect its black towers. The fortress looms atop a low plateau deep in the mountains. The view from its highest towers affords a panorama of the northern Thanelands and Hagreach.⁠
330690495:
Absalom Mint

The Absalom Mint, located near Azlanti Keep in Absalom's Wise Quarter that produces much of the city's coinage—a function that, due to the City at the Center of the World's outsized influence on trade and commerce, literally and figuratively shapes money across the Inner Sea region and beyond. Coins minted in Absalom are either accepted in locations as distant as Tian Xia and Vudra, or is the standard by which nations measure and mint their own currency.⁠

The Mint re-mints currencies from other nations, often increasing the resulting coins' purity in the process.⁠ Its building also houses the city's Office of Taxation.⁠
335086205:
Prada Hanam

Prada Hanam is a small port city on the eastern coast of the nation of Jalmeray. The settlement's defining feature is the Murmur Dome of Prada Hanam, an enormous, multi-building structure that suddenly appeared in the town centuries ago.⁠
342003495:
Chamber Grove

The Chamber Grove is where the Ivy District Council meets to discuss matters concerning, above all, the district's theater scene, as this is of paramount importance to the district. The fact that the building they occupy is a theater converted into offices speaks volumes about this interest and close connection to the arts.⁠
344906535:
Lasinavel

Lasinavel is a city situated on the north bank of the Kyonin River about 30 miles upstream from Iadara, famous for its countless feasts. The city was founded by Lasina, a renowned chef who wanted to create a place to host others.⁠

The kitchen is at the heart of Lasinavel culture, where magical processes create an environment in which food and ingredients remain fresh for a long time. Chefs are invited to prepare their dishes in the city's ovens.⁠ Although it boasts many festivals, none has become as famous as the feast in which Lasina created a dish resembling a dragon.⁠
397674445:
Shadow Caverns

The Shadow Caverns are located in Nidal's sinister Uskwood, not far from the capital Pangolais.⁠ On the surface they appear to be nothing more than a cave above an icy spring, but they conceal an entrance to the Darklands.⁠

Sihadrimon

Sihadrimon is one of the numerous prosperous coastal cities that dot the shores of the Betul Sea in the Western Ghats region of Vudra.⁠
401390565:
Nordein Glacier

The Nordein Glacier is located in the central Fog Peaks of southern Galt.⁠ The mountain on which the glacier sits contains a hidden valley that is slowly being swallowed by the ice. Legends claim that an evil spirit called the Jarl of the North Wind lived near the glacier.⁠

That legend turned out to be true because, when adventurers arrived at the glacier, they became trapped in a demiplane that they collapsed using the Vernal Key. Since the Godsrain, the growth of the glacier is beginning to threaten to consume the Fog Peaks in their entirety in a few years' time.⁠
402012345:
Spider's Nest

The Spider's Nest is crater several miles in diameter located as of 4713 AR in Irrisen. It formed in 4529 AR when a gigantic explosion shook the eastern Hoarwood Forest, and out poured plumes of smoke, fire, and giant spiders. Queen Yelizaveta sent her armies to defeat this sudden spider horde before it could spread much beyond the forest, and they succeeded. Few have explored the area since, and no one yet knows the cause of the original explosion.⁠
402594595:
Plumetown

Plumetown is the only major settlement on the island of the Smoker in the Shackles. Willa Cloudbuster is the de facto mayor of the town, and oversees Plumetown's sometimes impatient and disruptive visitors with a small army of constables: former pirates who carry massive clubs. The entire town seems designed solely to house, feed and entertain its visitors who seek the wisdom of the mysterious soothsayers, Keeba's Eyes, living in the caverns of Mount Keeba. It boasts a large number of taverns, hostels, gaming houses, and brothels.⁠

In 4717 AR Whark won the Free Captains' Regatta and was granted this town which she works to modernize into a hub of trade and entertainment.⁠

429259625:
Uiry Manor Museum

The Uiry Manor Museum was the residence of this noble family who held considerable influence in the city until 4673 AR. One night, a stranger arrived at the house, invited by the Scion Lord and when the butler went to another manor to get more wine, he returned to find a scene of carnage; everyone was dead, from the nobles to the children of the servants. The crime was never solved, and the family turned the house into a museum to avoid falling into poverty. Several guides explain the history of the artifacts and theories about how the murders might have occurred. Scion Lady Veridel was a schoolgirl when her family was murdered, and although she refuses to sleep in the manor, she also refuses to sell it for reasons that remain unclear.⁠

453237785:
Friendly Merchant

Despite its name, the tavern known as The Friendly Merchant is anything but. Located in the Shadow of the vast Irespan in the Underbridge slum district, The Friendly Merchant is run by an aiuvarin named Siov Cassimeel, who uses this ramshackle tavern as a front for petty crimes, but specialises in smuggling by using hidden docks attached to the tavern.

Siov rents out the docks to anyone willing to pay his high prices, though he drops the price for any member of the Night Scales. He is also rumoured to keep track on anyone using his dock and reports them back to the Night Scales.⁠
460982705:
Velecia Nora

Velecia Nora is an isolated snow-covered fort made of iron and stone in the Irriseni province known as the Verge. When a unit of soldiers demonstrates cowardice or disobedience, it is marched to Velecia Nora where it receives what is known as the Velecian Cruelty. One soldier in each group of ten is selected in random and beaten to the death by his nine comrades. The remaining soldiers form the new unit and return to duty. Necromancers raise the corpses of the killed soldiers and add them to the ranks of the Decimated, a small army of undead soldiers that drill eternally in the wastes southeast of Velecia Nora. The Decimated brigade is led by the graveknight General Fyodor Yelizaveta.⁠
465598305:
Slipcove

Slipcove is a small port on Bag Island in the Shackles.

The lord of Bag Island, Jolis Raffles, attacks the slave ships of Cheliax and offers freed slaves the chance to live on Bag Island. As a result, Slipcove has the largest halfling population in the Shackles.⁠
470339595:
Fields of Pain's Forgetting

The hidden Fields of Pain's Forgetting in Ombrefell are filled with bio-luminescent, hallucinogenic mushrooms, white poppies, the powerful analgesic flayleaf, and other plants that produce some sort of addictive pain-relieving drug. Some are intentionally poisoned to expose black-market sellers of pain-avoidant substances heretical to Kuthite beliefs, while pure specimens are distributed to religious and independent torturers. Mistress Cultivator Preali Dhat, a representative of the Umbral Court, oversees distribution and fulfills requests.⁠
481146985:
Butraf

Butraf is one of the numerous large, prosperous cities that dot the fertile Qadiran region of Pashman. It is located a few miles south of the banks of the Jackal River; the river forms Pashman's northern border with the neighbouring region of the Plains of Paresh.⁠⁠
488736685:
Baslwief

The mining village of Baslwief is located in the foothills of the eastern Fenwall Mountains in Varisia, on the banks of the Sarwin River.⁠
494866325:
Bank of Abadar

The Bank of Abadar is the name of the Master of the First Vault's temple within the Varisian city of Kaer Maga. Located within the city's walls, in the south-eastern part of town known as the Tarheel Promenade, the bank is one of the financial centers of Kaer Maga.⁠

The strongly fortified and ornately decorated building contains much of the city's liquid wealth, and its clergy work hard to make sure that bargains are kept, and contracts are properly maintained. They know that breaches of faith and the breaking of contracts can only lead to the end of the already quite tenuous peace within Kaer Maga. In this respect, the Bank of Abadar tend to emphasise his interest in law over his other aspects and the are work closer with the church of Asmodeus than many other temples do.⁠

In addition to witnessing agreements, bargains, and pledges, the members of Abadar's faith tend to the sick and wounded (for a nominal fee), and help to maintain Kaer Maga's magical sanitation system (for free).⁠
497116765:
Vasterborg

Vasterborg is a heavily fortified town in the Irriseni province known as the Verge. It is located close to the border with the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, and a large part of its population consists of soldiers, ice trolls, and winter wolves.⁠
505490225:
Peddlegate

The city of Peddlegate is located in the northeast of the nation of Druma, hard against the Five Kings Mountains.⁠
510580985:
Dallo

The village of Dallo sits in the western pan-handle of the nation of Wanshou where it nestles against the nearby neighbouring nation of Zi Ha and the looming Kelsang Mountains. Dallo is located almost as far from the storm-tossed coastline of Wanshou as possible, meaning the influence of Wanshou's evil kraken overlord, Zhanagorr, is as minimal as it can be. Still, Dallo is a village suffused with poverty.⁠ It is home to superstitious rice farmers, many of whom worship Malikeen,⁠ a samsaran who was a previous incarnation of Bakten Shengrah, who is said to have saved the village from flooding. Malikeen oversaw the construction of the most prominent feature of Dallo, it enormous dam.⁠ A stupa dedicated to Malikeen sits atop this massive dam and the waters it contains are used to feed the surrounding rice paddies.⁠

Adventurers, travelers, and goods leaving or entering Valashmai all move through Kutaban, enriching the local merchant lords. Though they typically feud with each other, these merchant lords unite to protect this status whenever an upstart trade city tries to compete with Kutaban for its monopoly on Valashmai's northern border.⁠

Kridorn

Kridorn is the second-largest city in Iobaria, passed only by its regional rival of Mirnbay. Located on sloping cliffs that rise above the Castrovin Sea, Kridorn's towers and lighthouse make it an easily visible landmark for sailors.

Founded in 905 AR, Kridorn was originally a small fishing town, but its growth was stymied by pirate fleets. King Iobar I attempted to drive off the pirates, but ended up perishing at the Battle of Kridorn in 937 AR. Hrugil, Iobar's son, repelled the invading corsairs, and spent the remainder of his reign improving Iobaria's fleets, resulting in Kridorn's growth into a booming port city by 975 AR. Kridorn was able to survive New Iobaria's collapse in 4659 AR, and became the destination of many Galtan nobles fleeing their nation's collapse into revolution.

Kridorn is considered one of Iobaria's safest cities, despite unreliable services and rampant corruption caused by its leader's thirst for conquest.⁠

The blacksmith here is Ukorviak, a shadow giant and the only one among the Xoskerik tribe who knows the secrets of forging living steel. Weapon sales are usually reserved for agents of the Umbral Court, though Ukorviak sometimes decides to sell to foreigners, provided they pay the exorbitant prices he demands.⁠

Dekarium

The Chelaxian settlement of Dekarium rests on the northeastern bank of Lake Sorrow near the mouth of the Tomarsulk River. Across Lake Sorrow lies Cheliax's capital, Egorian,⁠ while the Barrowood begins just west of the city.⁠⁠ The city is renowned for its highly skilled fishermen and abundant fey-blooded sorcerers. Local legend tells that the townsfolk of Dekarium are descended from nereids.⁠ A druid patrols the land between the town and the forest, mounted on a griffon named Ironwing Kazi, seeking out evildoers and those wishing to make sacrifices to their diabolic masters in the Barrowood.⁠ Much of the village secretly worships Gozreh, including its mayor Lalita Jireen, who manages the town's image and tithes to House Thrune.⁠

Castle Everstand

Castle Everstand is a large, abandoned fortification in the Gravelands, located just west of the northern reach of the Fangwood. Waunomani (pronounced Wau-noh-MAA-nee),⁠ also known as Silungan,⁠ is the closest thing to a capital in the archipelago nation of Minata, off the eastern coast of Tian Xia.⁠ The diverse and heavily fortified city serves as a center of sea trade on the eastern coast of Belem and port for Minata's defensive fleet of warships.⁠

"Waunomani" is a word of the Tau Nui people, a once-nomadic folk who claim descent from the ancient empire of Taumata and now primarily live in the Minatan isles of Rendah Pulu.⁠

Iron Rose

The Iron Rose is an opulent palace located in a verdant valley in the Menador Mountains of northeastern Isger, close to the border with Druma. Its mistress is Lady Kaltessa Iyis, the high priestess of the archdevil Mammon in the Inner Sea region. From here she directs her centuries-long plots on behalf of her infernal master.⁠

Blackjacket mercenaries guard the palace and protect the valley against attacks from Molthune to the north being situated in one of the few passages that directly connects the two nations.⁠
644005035:
Screaming Obelisk

A landmark of the Inner City district of Katapesh, The Screaming Obelisk is visible for miles around. The Screaming Obelisk is a massive spire nearly 400 feet tall and made of solid red carnelian.

The structure is covered in symbols; the one nearest the bottom seems to be times and date, while the higher, more mysterious symbols are unfanthomable. This does not stop people trying, and every year the Obelisk attracts scholars, linguists, engineers, and wizards from around the Inner Sea region who try to unravel its mysteries. The Screaming Obelisk's name comes from the holes cut into the top of it which, when the winds pick up, radiate an eerie series of whistling sounds.⁠

As well as an impressive tourist attraction, the Obelisk also serves as a giant sundial. Surrounding the Screaming Obelisk are three belltowers that use the shadow cast by the Obelisk to measure the passage of time, sounding a bell at every hour of the day.⁠
645643315:
Briar Henge

Briar Henge is a druidic gathering place in the Verduran Forest centered around a circle of magical menhirs. Many centuries ago, druids created a base of briar walls using magic around the structure, and over time, different druidic groups have used it as their base.⁠
645753435:
Rift of Niltak

The Rift of Niltak is a mist-shrouded canyon found in the Red Mountains of north-eastern Varisia. No one knows what the origins of the rift are, but all agree that it is filled with all manner of strange flora and fauna. Gigantic insects and centipede horrors can be seen crawling over plants found in no other place on Golarion, and the echoes of shrieking bat-like creatures reverberate off the glen's walls.

An accurate description of the rift has not come to light, as those who enter either never return, go insane, or kill themselves shortly after emerging from it.⁠⁠
660844935:
Ostenso

Ostenso is a major port city on the southern coast of Cheliax, just east of Cape Erebus, and is the easternmost city in the country.⁠ Ostenso is currently the home port of the Chelaxian Navy with grand, spacious docks.⁠⁠ The naval works here are the largest on the continent, making up a quarter of the city that sprawls over the water. Another quarter of the city stands upon a line of stones known as Custodisce Break, which stretches half a mile into the sea and forms the natural harbour.⁠
662400525:
Iudeimus Tenement

The Iudeimus Tenement is one of the numerous high-stacked tenement buildings that still litter Old Kintargo and house many of Kintargo's poorer working-class residents.⁠ Its residents are nearly equally split between short- and long-term stays.⁠

Like many such tenement buildings, it is run by a thoroughly disreputable manager, the hateful old crone Nurla Botve.⁠ The building is one of the taller ones in Old Kintargo and well built, with a bottom floor made of stone and top two floors made of wood.⁠
665591585:
Nogortha Necropolis

The Nogortha Necropolis (also known as the Necropolis of Nogortha) is a vast burial site located in central Andoran between the Arthfell Mountains and Nogortha Peaks, southwest of the city of Oregent. These barrow mounds are the final resting place of hundreds of barbarians who once inhabited the Arthfell Forest but who were finally defeated in 1707 AR by Taldor's campaign of western expansion led by General Khastalus.⁠⁠ Many of the burial mounds have been emptied by grave robbers or are being excavated by Pathfinders, although many also remain to be explored.⁠⁠
682339645:
Fort Inevitable

Fort Inevitable is a small town just off the Crusader Road, sandwiched between the West Sellen River and the Echo Wood. It is ruled by members of the Hellknight Order of the Pike,⁠ but is otherwise unclaimed by any of the other political entities of the River Kingdoms.⁠

City of Thorns

Temple of the Ravenous Moon

The Temple of the Ravenous Moon, originally just called the Temple of the Moon,⁠ is in the Terwa Uplands, in an area considered to lie within the Shackles.⁠ It is an ancient ziggurat constructed of a red-veined white stone.⁠

It gets its name from the carvings on its walls, which show scenes of mass sacrifices under a grinning, befanged moon. The savage kuru tribes which live in the region avoid the temple.

The Hurricane King, leader of the Shackles Pirates, has sent two missions to investigate the temple, but neither of them returned.⁠ It is rumoured that the Pathfinder Society may be preparing to send its own expedition from Nantambu;⁠ plus Hemdak Wavebaiter has called for adventurers to explore the temple in an attempt to garner himself favour with the Hurricane King.⁠

Ruwido

Ruwido is a hovel-village secreted away in the notorious Ustalavic county of Virlych where misbegotten, cast-out, mad, and deformed souls can find a home, hide their faces from the world, and find a modicum of peace and acceptance. The village is located in the western hills of the Ghorcha Pass close to the waters of the Barrow Run.⁠ The settlement is shunned by practically everyone, including patrols from Lastwall and Amaans, while the villagers themselves are suspicious of any strangers approaching.⁠ One of the few regular and trusted visitors to Ruwido is Azra, a mute cleric of Desna.⁠
714989505:
Whispertruth

Whispertruth is a small settlement of runaways located in the Vergan Forest of Razmiran. Paranoid of being discovered, they do everything they can to keep the location of their town a secret from the government.⁠
716366765:
Dragonsthrall

Dragonsthrall is the only settlement on the island of Dahak's Horn. The island of Dahak's Horn was chosen by the great dragon-priest Aashaq when she first came to the isles of the Shackles, for her loyal humanoid worshipers to inhabit.

Elsekulp is a large Taldan town on the banks of the Porthmos River, approximately 90 miles upriver from the capital, Oppara.⁠

Novoboro

It boasts a dozen timber buildings and a two-story stone tower, with archer lookouts on top watching the river on which the town is situated. The path to the town is marked by painted trees and tattered banners bearing the image of a crow. Crows are an important omen to the locals, and killing one is punishable by death.⁠

Rivercroft

Rivercroft is a fishing town located at the confluence of the Usk and Gjurn Rivers in northern Nidal.⁠ Besides fishing, the town earns some of its income from river tolls, placing it in a better economic position than other towns in the region.⁠

The town leader is Beldiore Chaintongue, who became interested in Rivercroft after a merchant discovered a shadow giant inside a massive shadowglass crystal and brought it to town. The shadow giant holds a book with runes similar to those found in Voyages into the Void. Beldiore has issued a call for adventurers to solve the mystery of this crystal and in the hopes of potentially earning a promotion for his efforts.⁠
771869845:
Marbledome

Marbledome is the central opera house of the Varisian city of Korvosa, and can be found in the upscale Heights District, just south of Castle Korvosa. Productions at the Marbledome, which is owned by House Jeggare, are always extremely lavish, but the operas performed there as of 4708 AR were often mediocre and rarely broke even.⁠⁠ Nevertheless, it is one of the centers of Korvosan high society, with wealthy families clamoring for the best box seats.⁠

As of 4708 AR, the Marbledome was (poorly) managed by Touran Palastus, a somewhat sadistic man who has driven more than one performer to relocate to Magnimar, or even the Sandpoint Theater.⁠
772730825:
Valley of the Pyramids

The Valley of the Pyramids, uncovered during a recent khamsin storm, is an unusual landscape of twisted, sand-carved canyons not fully seen since the time of the Four Pharaohs of Ascension. Rumors hold that the four pyramids contain magical portals that allow access to the extradimensional tombs of the Four Pharaohs. As of 4708 AR, artifacts from the tombs had already begun appearing in Sothis's bazaars.⁠
773282075:
Sunstone Cliffs

The Sunstone Cliffs lie in the very north-eastern corner of the Thanelands in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings in the foothills of the Stormspear Mountains range.⁠ The cliffs are famous for the gemstones found there called Thrain sunstones, unique gems that glow with a warm yellow light and whose flaws allow knowledgeable users to determine which way is north. Named for the prospector who discovered them, Thrain sunstones vary from smaller, inferior gems with the brightness of a candle to those that glow like a lantern and any jewellery made from sunstones will fetch huge prices across the Inner Sea region.⁠

Unfortunately, the Sunstone Cliffs are a very dangerous region since they serve as the hunting ground for large groups of trolls and even rock trolls making it particularly dangerous at night. Those who come here to prospect for Thrain sunstones have to harvest them with great stealth and in very quick runs lest they end up as troll food.⁠
774616305:
Seer's Home

Seer's Home, located on the western coast of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, is Icemark's capital but no more than a large village by population. However, it is the largest and only permanently inhabited Varki shelter, and home to the Varki Seers, wizened elders who have retired to this more permanent residence.⁠
788406975:
Burn

Located in the western part of the Keystone district, the area now known as the Burn was once home to the Varisian Council. When esteemed painter Goren Andosalu went mad and set his studio on fire, the fire spread to several other fine buildings in the area, killing over 48 people. Andosalu was never confirmed as one of the dead.⁠

This destruction so close to their home building caused the Varisian Council to change where it convenes.⁠ Between this and the ghosts of these 48 residents that are rumored to haunt the location, most locals avoid the area. A local group of cat burglars named the Gargoyles uses the old Varisian Council building as a headquarters.⁠
809780145:
District Courthouse

The District Courthouse for the Foreign Quarter is a stone building where its judges are renowned for their knowledge of foreign law, and most crimes are tried in its jurisdiction because they are committed by foreigners. The Sleepless Suns maintain a presence in the building, assisting as bailiffs when needed.⁠
821497305:
Flower Street Market

The Flower Street Market, which runs alongside Ivy District Park, is full of flowering trees and bustling activity. It's a wide street where carts and carriages can pass side by side, and it connects to the Wise Quarter to the north. In good weather, an open-air market sets up, selling fresh fruit, flowers, pigments, and products from trades such as blacksmithing, carpentry, and crafts. Local restaurants set up food carts to attract customers, and the Brotherhood of Abadar patrols the streets for thieves and checking merchants' licenses.⁠
826700655:
Seven's Sawmill

Seven's Sawmill is the oldest of the six major sawmills on Kyver's Islet in Magnimar and has never changed ownership. Production occurs here, but not in significant volumes, because it is used as the meeting place of the secret society called the Brothers of the Seven. Few know of the group or the meetings.⁠
828873985:
Moon Silver Pool

The Moon Silver Pool is located at the northernmost edge of the Arthfell Forest. Rumors exist that the pool was created by Narven, the druid king of the forest, though its purpose remains unknown.⁠

Franax, a port town located on the Lake of Mists and Veils, was once the centre of Iobaria's shipbuilding and repair thanks to its advantageous geography. 858365925:
Burning Brand

Burning Brand is a tattoo shop in Kaer Maga run by a man who only goes by the name of Bull. Skin Artists gather at the shop, which also serves as a sort of club for the gang. Scarification enthusiasts come to get all kinds of body art, which they proudly display on their bodies.⁠
864531295:
Castle Urion

Castle Urion is the first town most crusaders heading to Mendev up the West Sellen River see when the enter Numeria, but it is far from the typical barbarian settlements that are strewn across the country. This settlement is technically under the control of the Black Sovereign, but it is in reality controlled by an order of knights dedicated to Iomedae. These knights built Castle Urion as a way to protect and guide those crusaders sailing up the River Sellen (or "River Road" as it is often called) from Cassomir in Taldor to Chesed. This order of Iomedaean knights is particularly special, as they ride trained griffons, which help them patrol vast stretches of the river, certainly more than they could if they patrolled only on horseback.⁠⁠ The current commander of Castle Urion is Caroliss Minerran.⁠⁠
865759435:
Wellspring Tower

The Wellspring Tower is one of the aeon towers that Aroden placed around the Isle of Kortos.⁠ The tower is a 300-foot-tall mudbrick step pyramid with a flat 10-foot-wide top and four uneven tiers.⁠⁠

The tower is located on the north side of the Isle of Kortos, near the Verdant Passage⁠ and the small town of Matten Cleave.⁠ It is known for having a sweet water spring at its base that provides water and greenery to the surrounding area.⁠
873328385:
Emperor's Footprint

The Emperor's Footprint is a massive sinkhole in the southern Chang Liao Jungle of the Tian Xia nation of Po Li. It is a sight of religious pilgrimage, but it rarely visited because of the many dangerous creatures and hostile Sunsu Godae tribespeople who live there. Those who survive the journey to the Emperor's Footprint find that prayer and meditation connects one directly to one's patron deity in Heaven. A rare purple flower that holds resurrection or geas powers, and only blooms once every 144 years, is also said to grow here.⁠
880491645:
Castle Clarion

Castle Clarion was built in Katapesh by Oslynn Clarion, a now-retired explorer, about 4600 AR. A small set of docks, positioned under the cliffs of Castle Clarion, are used by the Clarion family for any shipping they may need to do and can hold nearly all of the Clarion fleet of ships (nearly a dozen blacksailed vessels). The castle, made up of slim towers that rise high above the castle, are connected by covered bridges. The sparkling walls and red roofs of Castle Clarion make it an easy landmark to spot from land or sea. Lord Clarion is loyal to the government of Katapesh and dutifully adheres to all of the city's laws and requests. He is also one of the city's largest merchant of slaves.⁠

Despite its elegance and lack of fortifications, the castle is well defended against Lord Clarion's many enemies, most notably agents of the Gray Corsairs. Traps riddle the castle and his servants include veteran warriors and mages. Also, due to Lord Crarion's ties with the Pactmasters, several aluum guard his property.⁠

Valas's Gift

Valas's Gift was a small town in the north of the nation of Mendev, located on the road north from Kenabres. Cecaelia Swirl

The Cecaelia Swirl is a waterfall on the island of Besmara's Throne in the Shackles named after a tribe of cecaelia who inhabits the roiling surf. Great Temple of Lissala

The Great Temple of Lissala, located in central Bakrakhan, was the largest and most famous temple of Lissala, the patron goddess of Thassilon, and home to the Chalice of Lissala, an artifact gifted by the goddess herself. The temple sank beneath the Varisian Gulf when Earthfall hit, and it is now home to Vanush, a kraken who uses the Chalice of Lissala to lure sailors to their dooms. 939875345:
Lady Docur's School for Girls

Lady Docur's School for Girls is the oldest of the many private schools in the Villegre district of Kintargo, but is somewhat overshadowed by the larger, more famous Alabaster Academy.

Lady Docur's School was founded approximately 300 years ago by its forlorn elven headmistress Lady Mialari Docur, who as of 4724 AR still operates the school.⁠⁠ She founded the school when educating young ladies in elven ways was fashionable. Tastes changed over the centuries, however,⁠ and as of 4724 AR its students are primarily female aiuvarins from across Cheliax, Isger, and Molthune.⁠⁠

The seemingly innocent school harbours a strange secret, however, for Lady Docur educates the most talented of her students in not only etiquette but also espionage. Those she deems her most promising students are recruited into a secretive organisation of spies and messengers called the Lacunafex that operates across Cheliax and often cooperates with the Kintargo-based Sacred Order of Archivists.⁠
949876935:
Mammoth Graveyard

The Mammoth Graveyard is a mountain valley in the eastern foothills of the northern Tusk Mountains, where mammoths near the end of their lives travel to die. The valley has grown into an intelligent genius loci, guiding mammoths to itself while confounding travellers, who only find it by accident and never twice. The formation of the Worldwound, however, corrupted the Mammoth Graveyard, and mammoths ceased coming there; it became home to bone golems and a massive flesh colossus made from rotting mammoth corpses.⁠

Evaren

The town is ruled by the Council of Three, the most notable being Councilor Pavla Trynar, regarded as the most powerful magic user in all of Iobaria. Trynar's many apprentices help to protect the town and keep the peace.⁠

Archstone Monument

The Archstone Monument stands near the western end of the Field of Concord in the Andoren capital of Almas' Liberty District. It was a gift of the gillmen, who gave it to the people of Andoran in 4670 AR in recognition of their embrace of freedom and equality after the People's Revolt. It contains the keystone of the famous Arch of Aroden, which the gillmen dragged to Andoran from the Hespereth Strait. The citizens of Almas often touch the keystone, believing it will give them good luck.⁠⁠
971182495:
Broken Shore

The Broken Shore is a mile-wide sea of hard black glass and sand that ripples out in concentric circle patterns located in the Algid Wastes, on the amorphous border between the northern Hold of Belkzen and the Realm of the Mammoth Lords. On its edges stand statues of forgotten gods, and it is avoided by both the Kellid tribes of the Realm of the Mammoth Lords and the orcs of Belkzen, who know it to be haunted.⁠
990862725:
Arazlant Mox

Arazlant Mox is the highest peak in the Kortos Mounts, the mountain range that dominates the center of the Isle of Kortos. It is over 26,400 feet in height.⁠ The peak was the first home of the Starstone when Aroden raised the island from the sea, and is sacred to all four Ascended gods.⁠
992929985:
Aspenthar

Aspenthar is Thuvia's second largest city-state and is the country's second port city on the Inner Sea after the capital, Merab. Generally seen as more dour in character than the capital, Aspenthar is under the rulership of the ambitious Prince Zinlo, who has decreed that martial training is mandatory for all citizens.⁠ Some worry that this training is in preparation for an invasion of one of the other city-states, or perhaps even an attempt to kidnap Artokus Kirran, the inventor of the sun orchid elixir.⁠

998583095:
Sleeper

The Sleeper is a gigantic monument located in the north-easternmost spur of the Mindspin Mountains within the Hold of Belkzen. It resembles an enormous dragon wrapped around a mountaintop. Steam or smoke seems to emanate from its massive maw, which is large enough to fit an entire house.⁠⁠

The sculpture contains a series of chambers coiled around the mountain peak that lead into its hollow interior. Beneath the Sleeper, deep in the heart of the mountain, is the ancient city of Xin-Gastash.⁠ The gigantic monument was the great entrance to the ancient capital of the Thassilonian realm of gluttony, Gastash.

Belkzen natives now call the sculpture the Sleeper. Only the bravest climb the mountain's slopes, much less enter the interior chambers. The local orcs, being naturally superstitious, stay away from the Sleeper and consider it a cursed ruin full of bad magic. The chambers within the Sleeper are mostly intact, although many of them show signs of earthquake damage.⁠
1007449015:
Port Ice

Port Ice, on the southern bank of the Lake of Mists and Veils in northern Brevoy, is a refuge for ruffians and lake pirates. While the city was once the capital of the former nation of Issia, it has been part of greater Brevoy since 4499 AR, when Choral the Conqueror united the region with its southern neighbor, Rostland. Even when Choral made New Stetven capital of Brevoy, Port Ice remained the seat of power of the conniving pirate lords of House Surtova.⁠⁠

When Choral's descendants in House Rogarvia mysteriously disappeared to a man in 4699 AR, Noleski Surtova, then ruler of Port Ice, leapt at the opportunity and took control of the nation in the absence of its traditional sovereigns and has since moved his court to New Stetven to the south.⁠

King Noleski's uncle, Domani Surtova, serves in the White Manor as Port Ice's current caretaker.⁠

The Port is often overcome by ice and snow in the winter months and sits closed, only visited occasionally until the spring's thaw. The summer months are spent frantically stockpiling supplies for the next winter.⁠
1013312705:
Rust Gate

The Rust Gate straddles the border between Kintargo's districts of Old Kintargo and Redroof and is the city's most heavily trafficked gate.⁠⁠ Most of the traffic crossing through it comes from the Ravounel Road, the busiest roadway in the city,⁠ which leads to Kintargo from the south and over the Argo Bridge.⁠
1023674425:
Temple of the Whispering Spider

The Temple of the Whispering Spider is a ruined temple of Lao Shu Po, located in Eryiu Forest of northwestern Quain,⁠ that is now inhabited by an enormous arachnid said to be the spirit of a cursed ancient priestess or royal maiden who rejected being sacrificed to have her heart become a celestial pearl.⁠⁠ Villages near the temple revere her as living testament of righteous defiance in the face of evil.⁠ They also say the arachnid is the only thing holding back the spirits believed to live within the temple⁠⁠ and leave regular offerings of silver, forage, and meat at its entrance.⁠
1024007905:
Shipmakers' Guild

The Shipmakers' Guild is one of the most powerful unions in Magnimar. They are based in the Beacon's Point district. It is owned by House Scarnetti, but Magnimar's navy has a somewhat permanent loan of a third of the shipyards, which is an increasingly irritating situation for the Scarnettis.⁠⁠
1048064905:
Trilmsgitt Towers

The Trilmsgitt Towers in Molthune are three towers, each within several miles of the others. They were built by three brothers, each of whom was a wizard, and are believed to be connected to each other by magic. However, nothing has been heard from any of the brothers for some time, and the towers appear to have been abandoned for some unknown reason.⁠
1048271275:
Mobhad Leigh

From the Shoanti term meaning "steps into hell," this perfectly circular pit is located at the base of the Kodar Mountains, on the Storval Plateau of northern Varisia, approximately 25 miles northeast of the source of the Aloren River. A set of spiral stairs run around the edge of the hole, but ends after only a few hundred feet. Beyond this point it is necessary to climb the sheer walls or fly. Few people know how deep the Mobhad Leigh actually is, although some rumor that it is so deep that it bypasses the Darklands region of Nar-Voth completely and opens directly into Sekamina.⁠⁠

Thunderblood Peak

The volcano Thunderblood Peak, formally known as "Thisskarshai", is the tallest mountain in the Chenlun Mountains. It gets its name from the frequent earthquakes that occur around it.⁠
1067237985:
Obelisk of Wonders

The Obelisk of Wonders is a mysterious ruined monument on the island of Kepre Dua in the Shackles. It is carefully guarded by the elven witch Kaala Raingold, who believes she receives revelations from it.⁠
1067816695:
Wailing Cave

The Wailing Cave is a half-submerged cavern in the Pangalley Atoll which is avoided by the pirates of the isle, who claim the ghost of murdered Black-Eye Benbem haunts it.⁠
1072655675:
Gecko

The Gecko is one of the ten remaining pilings of the Irespan in Magnimar. Standing 250 feet high, this piling is still connected to the bridge's deck. There is an entrance into the piling, but it is rumored to be haunted.⁠⁠
1090659945:
Magrevore

Magrevore is an enormous roiling magma pit located in the Darklands deep beneath the Qadiran city of Khoka. A portal at the heart of Magrevore leads to the depths of Malebolge, the sixth layer of Hell.⁠

Magrevore is guarded by a powerful nessari named Mardehzuk, a servant of the archdevil Moloch, who controls a far-reaching network of hryngar slavers that funnels a constant stream of slaves to be sacrificed in Moloch's name.⁠
1094611015:
Thrown Bones

The Thrown Bones is a gambling hall in Kaer Maga's unusual Ankar-Te district. Owned and operated by the Tian proprietor Hyu Zhuang, it has an assortment of gaming choices from the mundane to the exotic. Zhuang himself introduced many games native to his far-away homeland to Kaer Maga, including "Counting Legs," "Dragon's Breath," and "Stars and Crabs." Many of the servitors in the establishment are mindless zombies, something which does not stand out in this part of town. Those whom Zhuang trusts and respects are allowed into the back room where pit fights between undead servants are very popular.⁠
1098155185:
Rusthenge

The ruins of Rusthenge are located on Thunderhead Isle, a small islet near the town of Iron Harbor on Chakikoth Isle in the Ironbound Archipelago.⁠⁠

A cult of Xar-Azmak from Xin-Edasseril built it with the goal of obtaining sinful energy to [[Resurrection|resurrect] their demon lord, but Earthfall thwarted those plans.⁠
1101112415:
Penitentiary

The Penitentiary was conceived as a prison in western Corentyn where non-violent prisoners would be sent to silently reflect on their crimes, find inner peace, and be reformed upon release. Currently, it houses the city's forbidden religious relics and serves as a detention center for those who cause disturbances in West Drenches.⁠

The Penitentiary is one of the nine famous forts of Corentyn, the City of Nine Forts, according to the classical listing.⁠
1109135085:
Westcrown

For 800 years, Westcrown was the capital of Cheliax, and the rumored birthplace and home of the god Aroden. Known as the "City of Nine Stars", it was a shining example of the greatness of the Chelaxian empire. Westcrown was a classic, enlightened metropolis, even a rival to Absalom as a destination of religious pilgrimage and tourism. But then tragedy struck: Aroden died in 4606 AR, a bloody civil war swept over the nation, and decades of turmoil and strife plunged the city into despair.⁠⁠

The ascension of the House Thrune to the Chelaxian throne in 4640 AR cemented Westcrown's fate, as the capital was moved north to Egorian; no longer the City of Nine Stars, Westcrown now became the City of Twilight. The remains of the Chelaxian nobility huddle in Westcrown as a home-in-exile, as the city itself crumbles under the weight of mismanagement, crime, and a mysterious plague of creatures that hunt the streets at night.⁠⁠

In 4716 AR, Westcrown found itself the target of an uprising led by the Glorious Reclamation, an Iomedaean group of knights opposed to House Thrune.⁠
1110686775:
Nirfan

Nirfan is a Qadiran city in the south of the Maharev region, which is one of the safest and most fertile regions in all Qadira. Nirfan itself sits on the eastern bank of the Meraz River a few miles upriver of the town of Isa; the Maharev Jungle lies along the opposite bank.⁠⁠
1143759035:
Vault of Abadar

The Vault of Abadar, also known as the Bank of Abadar, in Absalom's Ivy District is the most holy site to the faithful of Abadar.⁠

While the Vault may appear to be unstable, it is sturdy and solid. Jostlin Ferqyr, councilwoman for the Ivy District, runs the vault like a merchant bank and provides venture capital to young merchants and artist groups.

Bor Dralfo, a paladin affiliated with Jostlin and the Vault, leads the Brotherhood of Abadar and enforces Ivy District rules to keep streets safe and clear, which has lead to tension with Nomarch Alain Always.⁠
1149201195:
Demgazi

Demgazi is a small Taldan town located on the Jalrune River in Sophra Prefecture,⁠ on the border between Taldor and Qadira, south of the Border Wood.⁠⁠ It is also across the Wood from the town of Heldren,⁠ and contributes inexperienced fighters to the High Sentinels.⁠
1154851785:
Gold Market

Gold Market is the largest marketplace in the city of Korvosa and the central attraction of the Midland district. Located between Eodred Circle and Eodred's Walk, people flock from across the city to visit its stalls and stands. Gold Market features local goods from not just Korvosa and it holdings but from across Varisia. The market is rife with food stalls of every sort, it has been speculated that as many as half the population of Korvosa eats here each month. One of the semi-regular features of the market is Sagitar Tiguan, a merchant who sells a range of trinkets and elixirs that he claims are magical. Whenever Sagitar's brightly coloured stall is there, adventurers are sure to be found nearby.⁠
1167305875:
Grundlescorn Lair

The Rovagug-worshipping hag sisters Grava, Mopple, and Polnivaar Grundlescorn dwell in a marshy section of Ravounel Forest known as Grundlescorn Lair, in a ramshackle hut partially built into the boughs of an ancient oak tree and supported by several crooked but sturdy stilts. The hut overlooks a low hillock in the marsh atop which the hags keep their cauldron and fire pit.⁠
1167332695:
Peacebound Isle

Peacebound Isle is the rough Common translation of the name of an island in the western outer reaches of the Eye of Abendego. It is a former site of the ancient cyclopean empire of Ghol-Gan, and was the home of the Peacebound Seers.⁠⁠
1178244775:
Razghora's Camp

A large number of displaced goblinoids gathered by the hobgoblin Razghora settled at Razghora's Camp in Druma.⁠
1180879375:
Ihalar

Ihalar is an underground city located between the Obari Ocean and the Meraz Desert. It is the westernmost example of the Khattibi-style underground settlements. The residents emerge only to graze their herds and trade with passing merchants. The city boasts many underground gardens sustained by the city's light wells although the lowest levels of the city have quietly been abandoned.⁠
1185303375:
Forae Logos

Also known as the Wise House and Library of Kortos, the Forae Logos in Absalom's Wise Quarter is the city's oldest and largest library, and one of the most extensive archives of written texts west of the Pit of Gormuz.⁠⁠⁠
1199278275:
Chalk Harbor

The grim mining town of Chalk Harbor is the only functioning settlement on Whyrlis Rock island in the Shackles. The town is the base of operations of the slaver Alahandra Boisich, rumored to have once been a powerful baroness of Cheliax. The ruthless Alahandra captains the barkentine Cloudbuster's Dream.⁠

There is no wildlife around Chalk Harbor save for bands of earth elementals and the few clusters of cullitox that lair underground, and no one can eat the sparse blighted crops that grow from the rocky soil. Water is drawn from the Elsewhere River, but all food is supplied by other islands and paid for by Alahandra.⁠
1200246785:
Rat

The Rat is one of the ten remaining pilings of the Irespan in Magnimar. Standing 250-feet high, there is an entrance near sea level and it is still connected to the bridge deck. Magnimar's least-successful Sczarni gang, Doolun's Lads, are based out of a series of chambers within The Rat.⁠⁠

Everforge is a tomb dedicated to Naika Omenspeaker near the now-abandoned Sky Citadel of Kravenkus in the World's Edge Mountains of modern-day Taldor.⁠
1219338415:
Merab

Merab is the largest of Thuvia's five allied city-states, and is the closest thing the land has to a capital city. It is ruled by Ilepodus, the Patron of Merab, and has adopted Sarenrae as its patron deity, whose Temple of the Redeeming Sun is the largest temple to the Dawnflower⁠⁠—or to any deity—in the country.⁠
1220453465:
Shotep-Kara

Shotep-Kara on the Scorpion Coast of Osirion was a military and commercial hub connecting Tumen to the Obari Ocean. The port city lost its prominent role after the death of the Four Pharaohs and the ruin of Tumen. A number of earthquakes and tsunamis finally drew the city into the sea in 1687 AR.⁠

Shotep-Kara's ancient monuments and temples are now part of the underwater ruins, and the place remains imbued with powerful magic. At the height of Four Pharaohs' reign, conjuration magic connected the port to the far corners of the empire and beyond. The magic is believed to persist to this day, though in wildly unstable form. Oceanic horrors and unquiet spirits infest the waters, but Shotep-Kara might still offer magical passage to faraway places, or even to other planes.⁠
1223572815:
Golden Aerie

The Golden Aerie is the headquarters of the Eagle Knights of Andoran, and is located at the center of the Field of Concord in the Liberty District of the capital city of Almas.⁠⁠
1236572045:
Katheer

Katheer, also known as "Glorious Golden Katheer", is the capital city of Qadira, and serves as the seat of power for the Satrap Xerbystes II.

The city possesses a canyon-like harbor and is the center of trade for goods to and from the distant Empire of Kelesh, as well as from throughout the Inner Sea. Each day, ships arrive from and depart for the major trading ports throughout the Inner Sea region, including Quantium, Absalom, and Katapesh. Katheer is also renowned as a center for learning, and contains dozens of academies of mathematics, philosophy, and healing.⁠
1247721105:
Bailer's Retreat

Bailer's Retreat is a rough and tumble tavern near Citadel Volshyenek in Korvosa's Midland district. Bailer's Retreat serves as a drinking hole for many recently released criminals as well as many members of the Korvosan Guard. Brawls between the two groups are not uncommon and normally result in the former convicts returning to jail. Still, Bailer's Retreat serves as a hotbed of rumours concerning every sort of illicit activity in the city.⁠
1249902695:
Grand Holt

The Grand Holt is a massive, multi-trunked fig tree located in the Green Ridge neighborhood of Absalom's Eastgate district. It is the oldest and largest tree on the Isle of Kortos, maybe even older than Absalom.⁠⁠⁠

The tree is tended by a fanatical druidic sect known as the Circle of Stones,⁠⁠⁠ who also care for Iolanthe, the immortal dryad queen who lives within it. The Grand Holt has expanded greatly over the millennia of its life, and entire blocks of buildings have been demolished to facilitate its growth. Blights, such as those caused by the Welt and the Tyrant's Grasp, have not been able to deter the tree's growth, and in fact seem to cause it to grow stronger. The tree provides a refuge for nature-loving adventurers, who are hired by the Circle of Stones to further Iolanthe's cause within the city and beyond.⁠
1268215625:
Temple Canyon

Temple Canyon is a mysterious site on the southern Tandak Plains, north of the settlement of Old Sehir.⁠ This long, dry canyon is over 30 miles in length and at times reaches several hundred feet deep. In the earliest days of Taldor, Temple Canyon served as a burial site for the nation's emperors, aristocrats, and heroes of legend. The buried wealth of Temple Canyon was almost entirely picked clean thousands of years ago but the now empty tombs still serve as a repository of Taldor's ancient history.⁠

Nowadays, the tombs of Temple Canyon are picked over by looters looking to carve away some of the ancient carvings and statuary in the vague hope of selling it on to Taldor's modern nobility. Lucky finds do still occur and in 4556 AR the tomb of Princess Modavora was discovered still intact, making the survivors of the expedition fantastically wealthy. Temple Canyon is considered a sacred site by House Stavian and the rangers who patrol its length happily execute any unauthorised intruders they catch within the canyon.⁠
1270082265:
Overlook

The Overlook serves as a palace, prison, and city hall for the city of Greengold. Multiple towers are connected by suspension bridges, giving an impression of magnificence to ships approaching the city.⁠
1276660855:
Corna Barracks

The Corna Barracks served the Westcrown Dottari in their operations throughout the Rego Corna district. However, during the anarchy of 4710 AR, it was temporarily abandoned and taken over by Hellknights who had deserted their posts. The Hellknights had allied themselves with the Council of Thieves, who promised to restore law and order to the city when they seized power.⁠
1278378765:
Gundrun

Gundrun is a recently reoccupied town in the revived nation of Sarkoris, located in the area previously referred to as the Worldwound.⁠ The people of Gundrun are descendants of the original inhabitants of the area, back when it was known as Sarkoris.⁠
1282907805:
Tyvas-Devas

Tyvas-Devas is an inland fortress town on the Devil's Arches island in the Shackles. It is made of stone by slave labor on the banks of the Holshod River. Arronax Endymion, the ruler of Devil's Arches, forbids outsiders from entering the town without his permission. The castle at the town's center is built as the admiral's redoubt should his Chelaxian enemies arrive.

Tyvas-Devas is overseen by Endymion's fiercely loyal lieutenant, Iome Paemadar. The black-clad summoner and her fearsome eidolon are known to walk the streets at night, making certain that everything is ready for her beloved admiral. The town is surrounded by rich farmland tended by slaves, which provides food crops for all of Devil's Arches. It is known that the admiral's great wealth lies in the cellars below the Tyvas-Devas' fortress.⁠
1292537285:
Elistia

The Hold of Elistia, or Fortress of the Bluffs, is a military outpost of the elven kingdom of Kyonin, located in the north-eastern part of the dwarven nation of the Five Kings Mountains.⁠ Elistia has a garrison of 500 elves⁠⁠ commanded by Lord Alavar.⁠

The Hold is protected by the Sentinels of Elistia,⁠ led by Lord Alavar in his role as Captain of the Sentinels.⁠ The Hold's elves are unfriendly to visitors, particularly orcs and dromaars,⁠ but assist mountaineers in need that they encounter in their patrols.⁠
1307977425:
Tomb of Emperors

The Tomb of Emperors is a ruin of the ancient Jistka Imperium located in what is today the nation of Rahadoum. It is situated in the eastern desert, beyond the Uta River,⁠ and is a destination for the Pathfinders of Swordmeet Lodge in Manaket.⁠

The Tomb of Emperors was a sprawling, colonnaded structure built at the Oasis of Xerapsion and it is known to have housed treasures made by famous Jistkan artisans. The Tomb was originally dedicated to the fifth ruler of Jistka Imperium, Inperantike Eraliskos, after her death at a decisive battle at Xeraspion—a battle that expanded the Imperium to the region east of the Uta. The nomadic tribes of the area became so impressed by the monument that a lot of nomads joined the Imperium army, forming an entire legion. Ancient Osirian invaders and their div allies looted the surface of the structure and most of its offering chambers during the era of the Night Plague but the Tekritani refused to further pillage the Tomb, leaving its lower levels and catacombs untouched.⁠
1312838685:
Minaret

The Minaret is a domed tower of humanoid construction located high among the Fog Peaks of southern Galt. Rarely glimpsed only through powerful spyglasses, the origins and purpose of the Minaret remain unknown to the people of the nation.⁠⁠

No one is aware that the structure is of Qadiran origin and that it was a poorly worded wish that trapped a noble inside of the tower and displaced it all the way up here.⁠

Eldentre

The town of Eldentre can be found in the south-western corner of the Linnorm Kingdom of Hagreach in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, on the banks of the Thundering River. The town is famous for the Lightning Oak, and the weapons that are made using the electrical energy from this tree.⁠
1363983765:
Frothripper

Frothripper is a waterfall about 200 feet tall that is fed from the Kortos Mounts north of Absalom.⁠

The waterfall hides an abandoned bardic college once known as Allegro College.⁠
1367581745:
Low Isle

Low Isle, along with its sister city of High Isle, provides much of the seafood for the nation of Xopatl. Located along the south-western coast of Xopatl on a small island in Lake Tapipallati, Low Isle is renowned for its seafood. The fishermen of Low Isle tend to remain nearer the coastline and fish for giant crabs, freshwater eels, and various other sea creatures.⁠⁠
1369500925:
Vale of Green Spears

The Vale of Green Spears is a forest of massive bamboo plants the size of redwood trees, planted 1,000 years ago according to legends by a wizard challenged by Tian Shen to plant 100 million trees. The reasons for the challenge vary by the legend's telling and include a test of the wizard's abilities and an attempt to house displaced birds.⁠

Harvesting the sought-after bamboo risks becoming the prey of the progeny of the late forest dragon Genseirin, who laired here and had long protected the old-growth stalks at the forest's center.⁠⁠
1375496505:
House of Oblivion

In Thuvia's interior desert lies the House of Oblivion. The towering structure was built over 7,000 years ago and was designed to lure Ahriman to Golarion. While the House of Oblivion is primarily built above ground, its various wings do not fully reside in the Universe.⁠
1375735215:
Etherveil

The Etherveil is a section of several acres in the Arthfell Forest, one mile south of Elberwick Rise, where only silver bark trees grow and a constant fog fills the area. During the solstices, the grayish fog turns blue-green, indicating that something more supernatural is behind it, and map-eaters who have gone there to map it return with completely different maps, although all agree on the elven runes found in the area. Legend says that lovers who declare their love within the fog will live happily ever after, and more than one lover has been lost in the forest searching for it.⁠

Klarwa Fountain

The Klarwa Fountain is located in the desert of western Osirion, in the region known as the Footprints of Rovagug.⁠ The site is a bowl-shaped depression filled with rain water atop a steep cinder cone from a long-extinct volcano, which rises hundreds of feet above the surrounding area. The water never quite evaporates despite the heat, and gases occasionally vent from deep within the cone. The violent plumes of water are sometimes visible from miles away, and one such column drew the attention of the anchorite Klarwa as he was dying of thirst in the badlands during the Second Age, giving the landmark its name.

As of 4714 AR the hill is used by the few travelers making their way through western Osirion, and its water makes the ascent up the steep hill well worth the effort. Some hermits live within sight of the Klarwa Fountain and hike up its sides when driven by desperate thirst, as anchorite holy Klarwa was.⁠
1431814015:
Breachill Town Hall

Breachill Town Hall serves as the office of the council as well as the guard for Breachill.⁠⁠ It is located off Monument Circle in the south of the town.⁠⁠ It contains rooms for all its members, in addition to a public hall used during the Call for Heroes and the town's courtrooms.⁠⁠
1433280105:
Red Pyramid

A prominent landmark within the Twilight Gate area of the city of Katapesh, the Red Pyramid is an ancient structure that dates back to the "Golden City" age of Katapesh.⁠ In recent decades, it also served as the headquarters of the Scarlet Triad.⁠

Pyramid of Kamaria

The Pyramid of Kamaria is the burial place for the Pharaoh Kamaria the Brazen, the only Osirian ruler to have openly worshiped the god Rovagug. It sits on the outskirts of the southern Osirian city of An, and dominates the settlement's southern skyline. The upper levels of the pyramid have long been cleared-out by tomb robbers, but are the home of a large cult of Rovagug; even they do not enter the lower trap-infested levels, however. The pyramid's central shaft dominates these dungeons, and it reaches all the way down to the Bloodcleft in the Darklands realm of Nar-Voth. A tribe of degenerate grimlocks is known to dwell near the shaft's base, and they occasionally trade strange artifacts and monstrous pets for slaves and food with the cultists above.⁠⁠⁠

The first major task of pharaoh Gebessek IX, after the assassination of his despised mother, was to exterminate every Rovagug cultist in the pyramid, the entire population of the city of An, and seal the sublevels of the pyramid with potent magic and wards.

In the reign of pharaoh Remeses IV the cult of Rovagug sought to return to the pyramid. Remeses IV initially dealt harshly with the cult, now known as the Cult of Rovagug Made Visible and led by Eshemel Bhalloc, but later decided it was better to allow them to re-establish themselves within the pyramid rather than have them organise elsewhere in secret. This policy has been followed by subsequent pharaohs.⁠

1747418845:
Hollow Garden

The Hollow Garden is a large entertainment module of the spaceship Divinity which was detached from its deck and slammed into Numeria, in the area now called Sovereign's Reach, during the Rain of Stars. It is currently run by Celmak Toysiel, a malfunctioning mannequin robot, who turned it into a trap for adventurers who have to provide 'entertainment' by traversing a dungeon customised by Celmak that only ends with their deaths.⁠

Celmak uses the entertainment module's remaining functional sensors to scan for potential victims. When someone approaches within a mile of the Hollow Garden, it begins to emit pulses and holograms (particularly idyllic gardens) to entice them. The doors to the bunker are always open with flickering lights, outwardly resembling a recently opened, malfunctioning, undefended section of the Divinity, ripe for plunder. Once the prey enters, the door seals and the only escape from that point is death; no teleportation is possible within the Garden.⁠

Celmak then greets explorers and explains that they are destined to make history; if they survive, then the rewards will be great, turning them into heroes rich beyond imagining. At the same time, it also scans their brains for their emotions and abilities, and analyses them to optimise the entertainment it provides, before opening the doors to the Hollow Garden. As its guests traverse the dungeon, fighting robots, and overcoming obstacles, Celmak records their thoughts and actions via hidden cameras, and crafts each encounter to test the responses of explorers, sometimes releasing psychoactive chemicals to 'heighten the drama', or offering commentary if its victims are having a too easy or too hard a time. Occasionally, a minor item from Celmak's hoard is given to its current victims, hand-picked to prolong the entertainment but never allowing success.⁠

In addition to Celmak and its robots, the Hollow Garden has recently become refuge to a group of demons fleeing the Worldwound. They accepted Celmak's offer to be occasionally sent into scenes as desired, but their leader Vlathherex found that they cannot teleport within the Hollow Garden, and now suspects that Celmak will never allow them to leave, and seeks to disable this lock.⁠
